newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian parties cancel meetings after violence.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian parties cancel meetings after violence.

text.p: Indonesia's two minority parties have cancelled some campaign rallies after violence involving supporters, the official Antara news agency and newspapers reported on Thursday.
The country's powerful armed forces have asked the three political parties contesting the May 29 election to stop taking out convoys during the campaign, the Jakarta Post reported.
"The (leaders of the) contestants should persuade their supporters to stop travelling in convoys during this campaign," Armed Forces spokesman Brigadier-General Slamet Supriadi was quoted as saying.

Thousands of supporters of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) and the ruling Golkar staged illegal parades in Jakarta and other parts of Java island on Tuesday and Wednesday, causing traffic jams.
At least one PPP supporter was killed in a road accident in the East Java town of Pasuruan on Tuesday while taking part in a procession, newspapers have said.
The government has banned parties from staging street rallies during the campaign to avoid clashes between supporters but both the PPP and Golkar have largely ignored the directive.

Only Golkar, the PPP and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are allowed to contest the May 29 election for the 425 elected seats at the House of Representatives. Another 75 seats are allotted to the military which does not vote.

Meanwhile, Antara said the PPP cancelled a campaign meeting scheduled for Friday in the city of Yogyakarta in Central Java, after a group of people smashed the windows of the party's office on Wednesday.

"We are afraid the emotion of the PPP supporters will become uncontrollable...the best decision is to withdraw our participation in the next round of the campaign (in the city)," said Syukri Fadori, chairman of the party branch in Yogyakarta.
Antara said the PPP cancelled a rally in Medan, North Sumatra, planned for Wednesday after three party supporters were injured in a clash with Golkar supporters on Saturday.

The PDI has also discontinued campaigning in Indonesia's second city Surabaya in East Java after about 5,000 supporters of the party's ousted leader Megawati Sukarnoputri stormed a gathering organised by a rival, government-backed faction.
Media Indonesia newspaper reported that the PDI also decided not to stage rallies in Ujung Pandang, South Sulawesi, on Wednesday for fear of violence.
